families.name: Access, Infrastructure & Interoperability
families.definition: Technical capabilities that determine whether a digital function is available, reachable, compatible, mobile, accessible, and usable under varying connectivity conditions.
families.includes: Include devices, network capacity, uptime, functional reliability, compatibility, interoperability, offline operation, and assistive-technology support.
families.exclusions: Exclude affordability and distribution rules, physical distance, and user skill.

families.name: Interface Choice Architecture
families.definition: Interface configurations that alter defaults, ordering, friction, prominence, simplification, active choice, and disclosure encounter.
families.includes: Include measurable UI states and interaction pathways that shape feasible selections.
families.exclusions: Exclude semantic content, recipient perception, and broad labels such as dark patterns when no atomic feature is specified.

families.name: Attention, Interruption & Temporal Control
families.definition: System features governing alerts, prompts, interruption intensity, delivery timing, automatic continuation, feed endpoints, and stopping cues.
families.includes: Include technological cue delivery and temporal interaction structure.
families.exclusions: Exclude prompt wording, attention state, habit, and campaign policy.

families.name: Algorithmic Curation & Adaptive Delivery
families.definition: Computational selection, ranking, amplification, filtering, personalization, and context-responsive delivery of options or information.
families.includes: Include measurable allocation weights, filters, personalization intensity, and update sensitivity.
families.exclusions: Exclude message meaning, user preference, and causal feedback-loop narratives without a specified system parameter.

families.name: Automation Reliability & Decision Support
families.definition: System performance and automation properties that determine what decision work is automated and how reliable recommendations and alarms are.
families.includes: Include automation level, decision-aid reliability, recommendation availability, and alarm error rates.
families.exclusions: Exclude human trust, automation bias, and institutional authority to deploy the system.

families.name: Human Control, Explainability & AI Collaboration
families.definition: Technical controls and interaction features supporting uncertainty display, explanation, verification, override, approval, and collaborative division of work.
families.includes: Include machine-confidence displays, explanation interfaces, verifiability tools, override controls, approval gates, and interaction-pattern flexibility.
families.exclusions: Exclude perceived control, trust, comprehension, and legal accountability.

families.name: Platform Social Affordances
families.definition: Platform action possibilities for visibility, persistence, search, replication, reach, association, identity disclosure, and editing.
families.includes: Include technical affordances that enable social action and information movement.
families.exclusions: Exclude the resulting network structure, norms, identity meaning, and content itself.

families.name: Digital Feedback, Rewards & Gamification
families.definition: Digitally implemented reactions, status metrics, rankings, rewards, streaks, schedules, and progress displays.
families.includes: Include technical feedback and reinforcement structures.
families.exclusions: Exclude social approval, intrinsic motivation, subjective progress, and reward policy outside the system.

families.name: Sensing, Monitoring & Traceability
families.definition: Technical capability to sense, log, display, observe, and reconstruct behavior or system events.
families.includes: Include self-monitoring, automated feedback, tracking visibility, third-party observability, and event logs.
families.exclusions: Exclude surveillance authority, sanctions, and perceived surveillance.

families.name: Human–AI Social Interaction
families.definition: AI interface properties that instantiate humanlike cues, reciprocal dialogue, persistent relational memory, affective response, and identity continuity.
families.includes: Include AI-specific interaction capabilities that can elicit social responses.
families.exclusions: Exclude the user’s anthropomorphism, trust, attachment, or felt social presence.

families.name: Immersion, Embodiment & Representation
families.definition: Technical properties governing sensory envelopment, avatar control, sensorimotor coupling, modality breadth, fidelity, realism, and remote interaction synchrony.
families.includes: Include mediated representation and immersive-system capabilities.
families.exclusions: Exclude felt presence, body ownership, identity meaning, and cultural stereotypes.

families.name: Privacy, Security & Identity Architecture
families.definition: Technical configurations controlling data collection, privacy choice, authentication burden, identity verification, access restriction, and retention.
families.includes: Include system-enforced privacy, authentication, authorization, and retention parameters.
families.exclusions: Exclude privacy concern, organizational policy, legal requirements, and threat intent.

families.name: Synthetic Media & Agentic Capabilities
families.definition: Technical capabilities for autonomous action, external tool use, synthetic-content generation, scalable production, representational fidelity, and provenance signaling.
families.includes: Include measurable autonomy and generative-system capabilities.
families.exclusions: Exclude the veracity or meaning of generated content, user belief, and institutional authorization.
